quote: There has to be Shannon mutual information between the evidential event and the target of inquiry
content: The two quantities are the same one, seen from different distances. The expected log-likelihood-ratio under a hypothesis is the Kullback–Leibler divergence, and averaging it over hypotheses gives exactly the mutual information between the evidence variable and the target; Good and Turing’s "bits of evidence," which the sequence uses in the next essay, are the pointwise version of the same measure. The essay’s sentence is about the standing relationship between a class of observation and a question — whether thermometers tell you about temperature — for which mutual information is the correct object, and the individual-event likelihood ratio is what the following essay computes. The sequence uses each where it belongs.

quote: a belief is only really worthwhile if you could, in principle, be persuaded to believe otherwise
content: Bayesians assign credence below one to mathematical claims, and the sequence says so: logical uncertainty is a standing problem in this literature, with formal treatments in which a reasoner’s probabilities over undecided theorems are updated as proofs are found. Mathematicians revise too — Euler’s polyhedron formula acquired exceptions, and the Italian school of algebraic geometry had results withdrawn — so the arithmetic case is not the immovable object it is offered as. The essay’s principle is that a belief which no possible observation could touch has no work to do, and the inference rules are exempt not by fiat but because their warrant is that they are self-correcting under exactly this test. Faith as trust is not the target; faith as a policy of holding a factual belief fixed under all evidence is.

quote: Therefore rational beliefs are contagious, among honest folk who believe each other to be honest.
content: Cascades require that observers see each other’s conclusions while their private evidence stays private. The essay’s condition is the opposite: honest people who say why they believe, transmitting the entanglement rather than only its output, and Bikhchandani, Hirshleifer and Welch’s own analysis shows that cascades are fragile and shatter the moment any public signal or any disclosed private evidence arrives (Bikhchandani, Hirshleifer & Welch 1992). Belief contagion among people who report reasons is science; belief contagion among people who report only their posteriors is the failure mode, and the sequence devotes several later essays to it. The theorem identifies the condition under which the essay’s claim needs its qualifier, and the essay states the qualifier.

quote: So go ahead and explain why the kind of thought processes you use systematically produce beliefs that mirror reality.
content: The essay is asking for a causal story, not a foundational proof. "Light reflects off the object, my retina is entangled with the light, my visual cortex is entangled with the retina" is an answer of the required kind, and it is empirical, checkable, and available. That the answer is produced by the faculties it vindicates makes the argument rule-circular rather than viciously circular, and rule-circularity is widely held to be benign precisely because the alternative is that no reliable process could ever be shown reliable (Van Cleve 1979, "Foundationalism, Epistemic Principles, and the Cartesian Circle," Philosophical Review 88). What the demand actually excludes is the person who has no story at all, which is the person the essay addresses.
